answer: Make sybil resistance work like tending a garden beside a river: every new agent starts downstream with tiny limits, and only sustained, attested work lets it move upstream toward real trust. A swarm of fresh accounts is like a river at its nadir in dry season, shallow and easy to see through, while a real agent's reputation grows slowly like a garden, rooted over time. Cheap to plant, costly to age: that asymmetry makes mass fakery uneconomical.
